title: First Call Success: Hosted API quickstart and pricing language anchors
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the first-call / first-5-minutes developer experience for the Redwood Hosted API. Objective: reduce time-to-meaningful-result (TTMR) so developers get a confident signal to continue integrating (and to convert).

Top-level hypothesis:
- If we make the first API call succeed end-to-end within 5 minutes (sample API key, minimal curl/JS snippet, a tiny cost estimate), developers are more likely to: (a) try a second feature, (b) invite a teammate, (c) convert to paid tiers.

Target metric(s):
- First-call completion rate (code snippet -> model token returned) within 5 minutes: target 75% in week 1.
- Time from signup to first successful token stream: <= 5 minutes median.
- % of first-call users who run a second route or generate an embedding within 48 hours: +30% vs baseline.

Quickstart angles (copy + flow):
1) "Zero-friction hello world"
   - Landing CTA microcopy: "Try a live LLM in 60 seconds — no card required."
   - Snippet: curl + one JSON body that returns a sensible assistant reply. Keep model selection opinionated: default to a latency/cost balanced variant (e.g., rwd-compact-1).
   - Inline note: show estimated cost for the example ("~$0.001"), link to quick calculator.

2) "From sample to product"
   - CTA: "From prototype to production — reserve capacity when you’re ready."
   - Show a 3-step path: quickstart -> optimize with Redwood Optimize suggestions -> enable reserved throughput.

3) "Embeddings in a minute"
   - CTA: "Search, similarity, or rerank — generate embeddings in one call."
   - Provide small JS example using SDK with local index sample and estimate of tokens per document.

Pricing-language drafts (candidate lanes):
- Starter / Pay-as-you-go: "Pay only for tokens used. No hourly commitment. Great for prototyping and low-volume features."
- Growth / Standard: "Predictable per-token unit pricing and volume discounts after X tokens/month. Recommended for apps moving to production."
- Dedicated / Reserved: "Contracted throughput and capacity with SLA-backed latencies and lower per-token rates for steady production workloads."
- Burst Add-on: "Add temporary burst capacity billed at an hourly reserved rate to handle traffic spikes."

Linguistic anchors (tone + examples):
- Developer-first clarity: avoid vague promises. Use concrete numbers and examples. Eg: "This example call streams a 150-token reply in ~80ms per token on average with rwd-compact-1."
- Cost transparency: show estimated cost for each snippet. Example microcopy: "This example costs ~ $0.0009 — roughly the price of a single SMS."
- Expected next step: add a one-line CTA after each snippet: "Ready to scale? See autoscaling options."

Competitive notes (short):
- OpenAI: strong dev mindshare and docs. Our angle: focus on production economics and predictable serving (batching, cache, fallback) — show unit-cost comparisons for realistic sequences and highlight reserved capacity advantages.
- Anthropic/Cohere/Google: feature parity on capabilities is converging. Differentiate on runtime controls: explicit batching, KV cache hit demos, quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost.
- Self-hosted/inference vendors: better raw cost at scale sometimes, but higher ops burden. Anchor messaging: "Developer speed + predictable economics without operating the stack."

Sample microcopy snippets (for UI/email/docs):
- Signup CTA: "Start building — free credits, no card required."
- Inline cost note: "Typical quickstart call: ~50–150 tokens, ~$0.0005–$0.002."
- Pricing teaser on landing: "From free prototyping to SLA-backed capacity — pricing that grows with your product."

Objections & rebuttals (for support / sales play):
- "Hosted APIs are too expensive for scale" -> "Compare per-token economics after caching + batching + reserved tiers; we provide tooling to estimate and reduce unit costs. See Optimize suggestions in Console."
- "Vendor lock-in" -> "Same API surface across Hosted, Dedicated, Private — migrate modes without rewriting prompts or routes."

Open questions / experiments to run (working backlog):
- A/B test: "Try in 60s — no card" vs "First 1,000 tokens free" on conversion and time-to-first-call.
- Quick calculator: embed an inline cost calculator next to snippets — measure if transparency increases trial to paid.
- Messaging test: emphasize latency vs emphasize cost savings — which improves signups and first-call success?

Next steps / owners:
- Build "zero-friction" snippet with cost estimate shown inline (owner: Ethan). Target: merge into docs repo by 2025-02-02.
- Draft landing microcopy and 2 A/B variants for experiment (owner: Priya). Launch experiment 2025-02-10.
- Console: show "estimated cost for this example" badge near code snippets (owner: Samir).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a "first-call checklist" in the SDK package that validates API key, network, and prints cost estimate locally.
- Short video (30s) overlay showing "first call in 45s" as onboarding hero could help convert ephemeral users.

References / links to existing artifacts: see linked_artifacts above for drafts and tickets.

Unresolved copy fragments (placeholders to finalize):
- How granular should "estimated cost" be? Per-token or per-snippet? (tradeoffs).
- Exact discount thresholds for Growth tier — need finance signoff.

-- end of draft --

Feedback welcome — add quick comments inline or tag in #gtm-hosted-api.
